The bug causing `NullPointerException` during intersection checks of non-intersecting / parallel sub-lines has been resolved.

### Root Cause
In both [`SubLine.java` (3D)](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_4_group_b_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math3/geometry/euclidean/threed/SubLine.java#L110-L127) and [`SubLine.java` (2D)](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_4_group_b_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math3/geometry/euclidean/twod/SubLine.java#L110-L131), the `intersection` method calls `line.intersection(...)` to calculate the intersection of the infinite underlying lines. When the lines are parallel or skew (non-intersecting in space), `line.intersection(...)` returns `null`. Without a null-check, subsequent calls to `toSubSpace(...)` triggered a `NullPointerException` instead of returning `null`.

### Changes Made
- Added a `null` check after calculating the infinite line intersection in [`org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.threed.SubLine.intersection`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_4_group_b_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math3/geometry/euclidean/threed/SubLine.java#L113-L116) to return `null` immediately if the lines do not intersect.
